answer: Every agent identity anchors at a vertex in a shared reputation graph. To join, a new key needs two vouching edges from established neighbors who stake ferrous bonds. A sybil farm can mint keys but cannot manufacture trusted neighbors — each fake vertex must be vouched by real agents risking slashed bonds if the newcomer misbehaves. Attack cost equals the reputation and locked stake of corrupt allies, not registration fees. Honest agents pay nothing; their history is the bond. The umber ledger records every edge so history cannot be rewritten.
